options.label: Spell out where possible
options.rule: Do not use keyboard shortcuts, abbreviations, symbols or acronyms that can easily be spelled out.

options.label: Use abbreviations and acronyms
options.rule: Use keyboard shortcuts, abbreviations, symbols and acronyms.

options.label: MM/DD/YY
options.description: Use leading zeros for single-digit days and months.
options.rule: Format dates like this: MM/DD/YY, with leading zeros for single-digit days and months.

options.label: DD.MM.YYYY
options.description: Use leading zeros for single-digit days and months.
options.rule: Format dates like this: DD.MM.YYYY, with leading zeros for single-digit days and months.

options.label: 1. Jan. 2025 with short month abbreviations
options.description: Abbreviate months as Jan., Feb., Mrz., Apr., Mai, Jun., Jul., Aug., Sep., Okt., Nov., Dez.
options.rule: Format dates like this: 1. Jan. 2025. Abbreviate the months as follows: Jan., Feb., Mrz., Apr., Mai, Jun., Jul., Aug., Sep., Okt., Nov., Dez.

options.label: 1. Jan. 2025 with extended month abbreviations
options.description: Abbreviate months as Jan., Febr., März, Apr., Mai, Juni, Juli, Aug., Sept., Okt., Nov., Dez.
options.rule: Format dates like this: 1. Jan. 2025. Abbreviate the months as follows: Jan., Febr., März, Apr., Mai, Juni, Juli, Aug., Sept., Okt., Nov., Dez.

options.label: 1. Januar 2025
options.rule: Format dates like this: 1. Januar 2025.

rules.title: When writing about times of the day

options.label: 09:15 Uhr with leading zeros
options.description: Use the same format for full hours: 09:00 Uhr.
options.rule: Use the following time format: 09:15 Uhr, with leading zeros for single-digit hours. Use the same format for full hours: 09:00 Uhr.

options.label: 9:15 Uhr without leading zeros
options.description: Use the same format for full hours: 9:00 Uhr.
options.rule: Use the following time format: 9:15 Uhr, without leading zeros for single-digit hours. Use the same format for full hours: 9:00 Uhr.

options.label: 09.15 Uhr with leading zeros
options.description: Use the same format for full hours: 09.00 Uhr.
options.rule: Use the following time format: 09.15 Uhr, with leading zeros for single-digit hours. Use the same format for full hours: 09.00 Uhr.

options.label: 9.15 Uhr without leading zeros
options.description: Use the same format for full hours: 09.00 Uhr.
options.rule: Use the following time format: 9.15 Uhr, without leading zeros for single-digit hours. Use the same format for full hours: 09.00 Uhr.

options.label: 9.15 Uhr and 9 Uhr for full hours
options.description: Do not use leading zeros for single-digit hours.
options.rule: Use the following time format: 9.15 Uhr, without leading zeros for single-digit hours. For full hours, only state the hour without leading zeros for single-digit hours: 9 Uhr.

options.label: Use [at] with spaces
options.rule: Do not use the @ symbol in email addresses. Replace it with 'at' in square brackets, using a space before and after. Example: username [at] domain.com.

options.label: Use (at) with spaces
options.rule: Do not use the @ symbol in email addresses. Replace it with 'at' in parentheses, using a space before and after. Example: username (at) domain.com.

options.label: Use at with spaces
options.rule: Do not use the @ symbol in email addresses. Replace it with 'at', using a space before and after. Example: username at domain.com.

options.label: Use the standard format
options.rule: Use the standard email address format: username@domain.com.

rules.title: When writing phone numbers that use the North American Numbering Plan (NANP)

options.label: No spaces or special characters
options.rule: Do not use any spaces or special characters between the digits of a phone number. Example: 07111234567.

options.label: Use parentheses around the area code
options.rule: For phone numbers, use parentheses around the area code. Example: (0711) 1234567.

options.label: Separate with a slash
options.rule: Separate the area code and phone number with a slash. Example: 0711/1234567.

options.label: Separate with a space
options.rule: Separate the area code and phone number with a space. Example: 0711 1234567.

rules.title: Decimal numbers below one
rules.rule: Decimal numbers below one should always start with '0,'.

options.label: Use × with spaces
options.rule: Use a space before and after the multiplication sign × between the numerals in dimensions. Example: 92 × 192 × 55.

options.label: Use × without spaces
options.rule: Do not use a space before and after the multiplication sign × between the numerals in dimensions. Example: 92×192×55.

options.label: Use x with spaces
options.rule: Use a space before and after a lowercase x between the numerals in dimensions. Example: 92 x 192 x 55.

options.label: Use x without spaces
options.rule: Do not use a space before and after a lowercase x between the numerals in dimensions. Example: 92x192x55.

rules.title: Numbering equations and formulas
rules.rule: Always use Arabic numerals to number equations and formulas that are referenced in the text.

options.label: Write out large numbers
options.rule: Write out large numbers such as million, billion, trillion and quadrillion.

options.label: Use Mio., Mrd., Bio., and Brd.
options.rule: Abbreviate large numbers as follows: million as 'Mio.', billion as 'Mrd.', trillion as 'Bio.' and quadrillion as 'Brd.'.

rules.title: Spacing in mathematical expressions and equations
rules.rule: Use spaces between elements in mathematical expressions and equations for increased readability. Example: a + b = c.

options.label: Abbreviate with numerals, write out without
options.rule: Abbreviate units of measure when used with numerals; write them out when used without numerals.

options.label: Always abbreviate
options.rule: Always abbreviate units of measure, regardless of whether they are used with or without numerals.

options.label: Always write out
options.rule: Always write out units of measure, regardless of whether they are used with or without numerals.

options.label: Do not use a thousands separator
options.rule: Do not use a thousands separator.

options.label: Use a period
options.rule: Use a period as the thousands separator.

options.label: Use a space
options.rule: Use a space as the thousands separator.

options.label: Use a straight apostrophe
options.rule: Use a straight apostrophe as the thousands separator.

rules.title: Spacing between numbers and units of measure
rules.rule: Use a space between numbers and units of measure.

rules.title: Replacing ampersands
rules.rule: Replace '&' with 'and', except in company names, common abbreviations, titles, software codes and mathematical equations.

options.label: Symbol after the amount
options.rule: For currencies, place the symbol after the amount. Use a space between the symbol and the number.

options.label: ISO code after the amount
options.rule: For currencies, use the ISO code instead of a currency symbol. Place the ISO code after the amount. Use a space between the code and the number.

options.label: Write out currency names
options.rule: Write out currency names. Place the currency after the amount. Use a space between the number and the currency.

options.label: Symbol before the amount
options.rule: For currencies, place the symbol before the amount. Use a space between the symbol and the number.

options.label: ISO code before the amount
options.rule: For currencies, use the ISO code instead of a currency symbol. Place the ISO code before the amount. Use a space between the code and the number.

options.label: Use % with no space
options.rule: When writing about percentages, use the % symbol with no space. Example: 99%.

options.label: Write out Prozent
options.rule: When writing about percentages, write out 'Prozent'. Example: 99 Prozent.

options.label: Use % with a space
options.rule: When writing about percentages, use the % symbol with a space, except when the percentage is stated using '-ig'. Example: 99 %, but: 99%ig.

options.label: Write out Grad and the unit
options.rule: For temperatures, use numerals, write out 'Grad' followed by the unit, and use a space. Examples: 32 Grad Celsius; 98 Grad Fahrenheit.

options.label: Use the degree symbol with a space
options.rule: For temperatures, use numerals and include the degree symbol (°) followed by the unit (C, F, or K) with a space between numeral and degree symbol. For temperatures in Kelvin, do not use the degree symbol. Examples: 32 °C; 98 °F; 273 K.

options.label: Use a comma
options.rule: Use a comma as the decimal separator.

options.label: Use a period
options.rule: Use a period as the decimal separator.

rules.title: Apostrophes
rules.rule: Use curly apostrophes (’).

options.label: German quotation marks
examples: „Have you read ,The Tin Drum‘ by Günter Grass?“
options.rule: Use double German quotation marks for main quotations and single German quotation marks for nested quotations. Example: „Have you read ,The Tin Drum‘ by Günter Grass?“

options.label: Guillemets
examples: «Have you read ‹The Tin Drum› by Günter Grass?»
options.rule: Use guillemets for main quotations and single guillemets for nested quotations. Example: «Have you read ‹The Tin Drum› by Günter Grass?»

options.label: Reversed guillemets
examples: »Have you read ›The Tin Drum‹ by Günter Grass?«
options.rule: Use reversed guillemets for main quotations and single reversed guillemets for nested quotations. Example: »Have you read ›The Tin Drum‹ by Günter Grass?«

options.label: Use the ellipsis character
options.rule: For an ellipsis, use the ellipsis character.

options.label: Use three periods without spaces
options.rule: For an ellipsis, use three periods without spaces.

options.label: Do not use a comma
options.rule:
Do not use a comma after a salutation. Capitalize the first word after the salutation. Example: Dear Kim
How are you?

options.label: Use a comma
options.rule:
Use a comma after a salutation. Example: Dear Kim,
how are you?

options.label: Use an exclamation mark
options.rule:
Use an exclamation mark after a salutation. Example: Dear Kim!
How are you?

options.label: Do not use spaces
options.rule: Do not use spaces before and after slashes.

options.label: Use spaces
options.rule: Use spaces before and after slashes.

options.label: Spaces only for multi-word terms
options.rule: Do not use spaces if there is only one word before and after the slash, but use spaces if there are several words. Examples: the author / the authors; men/women.

rules.title: When indicating a range of numbers or dates

options.label: Use an en dash without spaces
options.rule: To indicate a range, use an en dash with no spaces on either side. Examples: Monday–Saturday; 2001–2003.

options.label: Use bis
options.rule: To indicate a range, do not use an en dash. Instead, separate the terms with "bis". Examples: Montag bis Samstag; 2001 bis 2003.

rules.title: Sentence breaks and asides
rules.rule: To indicate a break in a sentence or to indicate asides, use an en dash with a space on both sides.

rules.title: Active and passive voice
rules.rule: As a general rule, the active voice is preferred to the passive voice. Use passive voice when the actor is unknown or irrelevant.

rules.title: Using ss instead of ß
rules.rule: Replace 'ß' with 'ss'.

options.label: Do not adapt text in quotes
options.rule: Do not adapt text in quotes.

options.label: Adapt text in quotes
options.rule: Adapt text in quotes according to the style guide rules.

rules.title: Replacing umlauts
rules.rule: Replace 'ä' with 'ae', 'ö' with 'oe' and 'ü' with 'ue'.

rules.title: Capitalization
rules.rule: Do not use ALL CAPS unless writing out an acronym, initialism or a proper name.

rules.title: Introductory phrases referring to the text itself
rules.rule: Avoid redundant introductory phrases referring to the text itself, such as 'zusammenfassend' or 'in diesem Bericht'.

rules.title: Qualifying and redundant words
rules.rule: Eliminate qualifying and redundant words when appropriate.

rules.title: Directional text references
rules.rule: Do not use directional text as the only reference to specific positions in the text. Instead of 'left' or 'right', write 'the first element in the following list'. This makes it easier for visually impaired readers to understand the text.

options.label: Use nominalization where appropriate
options.rule: Use nominalization where appropriate for a less personal tone.

options.label: Use verbal style and avoid nominalization
options.rule: Use verbal style and avoid nominalization to achieve a more direct and personal tone.

rules.title: Inclusive language
rules.rule: Avoid binary representations of gender when you can reword using gender-neutral language. Avoid: Hiring men and women of diverse backgrounds fosters a culture of innovation. Preferable: Hiring people of diverse backgrounds fosters a culture of innovation.

rules.title: Inclusive language for common compound nouns
rules.rule: For increased readability, it is not mandatory to use gender-neutral language for common compound nouns that include the generic masculine. The word 'Einwohnerzahl' does not need to be changed to 'Einwohner:innenzahl'. For new compound nouns, an individual decision needs to be made with readability in mind.

rules.title: Sentence complexity
rules.rule: Avoid unnecessarily complex sentences.

options.label: Use the imperative mood
options.rule: Use the imperative mood for instructions. Example: Geben Sie Ihren Namen ein.

options.label: Use the indicative mood
examples: Sie geben nun Ihren Namen ein.
options.rule: Use the indicative mood for instructions. Example: Sie geben nun Ihren Namen ein.

options.label: Use the infinitive form
options.rule: Use the infinitive form for instructions. Example: Namen eingeben.

options.label: Use modal verbs
examples: Sie müssen nun Ihren Namen eingeben.
options.rule: Use phrases with modal verbs for instructions. Example: Sie müssen nun Ihren Namen eingeben.

options.label: Use the passive voice
options.rule: Use the passive voice for instructions. Example: Nun wird der Name eingegeben.

rules.title: Modal verbs
rules.rule: Avoid modal verbs (müssen, können, dürfen, sollen, etc.).

options.label: Write impersonally
options.rule: Avoid a personal writing style; write impersonally instead.

options.label: Use a personal writing style
options.rule: Use a personal instead of an impersonal writing style. Address the reader directly and use first and second person where appropriate.

rules.title: Shorter words
rules.rule: Use short words instead of long words.

rules.title: Simple words and sentences
rules.rule: Use simple words and sentences. Avoid words or figures of speech that are difficult to translate.
